stem: A trading platform's matching engine speaks a custom TCP protocol, needs the lowest achievable added latency between clients and matching servers, and needs one static IP address per Availability Zone for clients to hard-code.

choices.text: Deploy an Application Load Balancer with path-based routing rules
Split traffic across two target groups using Route 53 weighted routing
Deploy a Classic Load Balancer for the matching engine
Deploy a Network Load Balancer in front of the matching servers

rationale: A Network Load Balancer operates at the connection level with minimal added latency, handles a custom TCP protocol without inspecting it, and exposes one static IP per Availability Zone, matching every part of the requirement. An Application Load Balancer's path-based routing adds Layer 7 processing overhead that is unnecessary for a custom TCP protocol and does not by itself provide a static per-AZ IP. Route 53 weighted routing splits traffic at the DNS layer between target groups; it does not change what either load balancer does with a connection and adds nothing toward the latency or static-IP requirement. A Classic Load Balancer is the previous generation of Elastic Load Balancing and does not match a current Network Load Balancer's throughput and latency profile.
